title.narrative: North-South Power Transmission Enhancement Project (formerly Power Distribution Project)

description.narrative:
The project will construct a 500-kV transmission line about 225 km long across the Hindukush mountain range between the northern town of Dashte Alwan and Kabul, at the southern end. It will include a new 500-kV / 220-kV substation to connect to the grid in Kabul, Afghanistan's capital. The project will add 1,000-1,300 MW to the existing 300 MW of transmission capacity between northern and southern Afghanistan. The new line will transmit electricity produced domestically by hydropower and fossil fuel generation in the country's northern region, as well as accommodate power imports from neighboring Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan to supply Afghanistan's domestic needs. The project will complement a second ADB power project under the proposed tranche 5 of ADB's Energy Sector Development Investment Program to build a 500-kV substation to connect to the grid at the northern end of the line in Dashte Alwan.
The Project is ranked as the top priority in Afghanistan Power Sector Masterplan (2012-32) as well as in the National Energy Supply Program (NESP) of the Government of Afghanistan.

Power shortfall in Kabul reduced from 100 MW in 2013 to 50 MW in 2020 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The power shortfall will be abridged in Kabul upon the completion of 500 kV transmission lines and associated substations that are financed under the North-South Power Transmission Enhancement Project (G0374/0375) and MFF2 Tranche 1 (G0464/0465) with the-then-expected completion by Q3 2022. The expected completion will be delayed due to the change of government in mid-August 2021 and the stoppage of work.
MFF1 Tranche 4 (G0332) and Tranche 5 (G0377) were completed on 28 November 2020 and 28 May 2020, respectively. The MFF2 Tranche 1 (G0464/0465) project achievement will be delayed due to the change of the government. The contractors and consultants have stopped their works since mid-August 2021. The contractors and consultants have stopped work. As per the approved approach paper “Afghanistan 2021 Situation: Proposed Actions and Next Steps” ADB has paused its operations.
The contracts for the 500 kV transmission line from Dasht-e-Alwan to Kabul (Arghandy) and 500/220/20 kV Arghandy substation were awarded on 7 June 2016 and 11 December 2017, respectively.
The associated packages of 500 kV transmission lines: (i) 500 kV from TKM border to Sheberghan was awarded on 17 Nov 2015 and completed on 21 October 2020, and (ii) 500 kV Sheberghan to Dasht-e-Alwan transmission line was awarded on 19 November 2017 and was expected to be completed on 14 November 2021 (the completion will be delayed due to change of government in mid-August 2021). These packages are financed under MFF1 Tranche 4 (G0332) and MFF2 Tranche 1 (G0464/0465). Data Source: Afghanistan CSO publications
